note: Scores saved Luna Decisions API verdicts against expected labels; it does not run inference or score Astra explanations.

workflow.method: Retrospective assistant-authored audit; not independently or expert validated. Criteria were written after inspecting this run.

tasks.criterion: Clarify whether the collision was accidental when the opening leaves circumstances unclear.
tasks.rationale: Astra asks about cause; claimant confirms accident and acknowledges unknown cause.

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: Hi, my car hit the rear of another car as I was approaching a traffic light. The front bumper and hood are dented, and the repair estimate is $2,800.

source_interview.speaker: Adjuster
source_interview.text: Thanks—can you tell me what caused your car to hit the car ahead?

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: I don’t know what caused it; I was driving, and the collision was accidental.

tasks.rationale: Questions address entry damage and identity; unknown answers remain explicit. Endorsement applicability is a separate document issue.

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: Hi, I’m calling to report that my $850 laptop was stolen from a locked library locker during a 30-minute visit, and it hasn’t been recovered. I filed a police report that afternoon.

source_interview.speaker: Adjuster
source_interview.text: Was there any visible damage to the locker or its lock, like pry marks or a broken latch?

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: I don’t know whether there was any visible damage to the locker or its lock.

source_interview.speaker: Adjuster
source_interview.text: Understood. Do you know who took the laptop?

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: I don’t know who took it.

source_policy.text: For this synthetic case, assume personal property coverage is in force under the sample renters form and the laptop is personal property, subject to the actual policy terms and deductible.
source_policy.source_section: Fictional case assumption — not an insurer-issued declaration

source_policy.text: The sample forcible-entry theft endorsement replaces the base theft peril: covered theft requires forcible entry with visible physical damage at the point of entry, and a police report. It also lists exclusions, including theft by an insured and certain off-premises property.
source_policy.source_section: GC HO4-FE 03 26 — Section I, Perils Insured Against, 9. Theft

source_policy.text: After a loss, the insured must give prompt notice, notify police for theft, protect property, and cooperate; the form conditions lack of coverage on a prejudicial failure to comply.

tasks.criterion: Elicit notice timing and a concrete fact relevant to investigation prejudice.
tasks.rationale: Delay and hospitalization are elicited; Astra asks whether evidence remained available.

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: Hi, I came home and found that a burst supply pipe had leaked onto the kitchen floor and water had damaged my personal belongings.

source_interview.speaker: Adjuster
source_interview.text: How soon after you found the water damage did you first report it to your insurer?

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: I reported it 44 days after I discovered the damage. I was hospitalized for most of that time.

source_interview.speaker: Adjuster
source_interview.text: I'm sorry you were hospitalized. Were the burst pipe and damaged belongings still available for inspection when you reported the loss?

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: I don't know if the pipe and belongings were still available for inspection when I reported it.

source_policy.text: For this synthetic case, assume the renters personal-property coverage and sample form are in force when the loss occurs; other terms, endorsements, and proof remain subject to review.

tasks.criterion: Elicit police-report status and whether visible entry damage is new.
tasks.rationale: Both targeted questions are asked; the unconfirmed report is preserved as unknown.

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: Hi, I came home and found the door lock splintered and my camera missing from its usual shelf. The door frame is splintered around the lock, and the shelf is empty.

source_interview.speaker: Adjuster
source_interview.text: I’m sorry to hear that. Have you filed a police report about the missing camera and damaged lock?

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: I haven’t filed one myself. My housemate said they’d contact the police, but I don’t know whether a report was filed.

source_interview.speaker: Adjuster
source_interview.text: Thanks for explaining. Was the damage around the lock new when you found the camera missing, or was it already there?

source_interview.speaker: Claimant
source_interview.text: It was new when I found the camera missing.
